hypotheses.binder: (hskew₁ : ∀ x ∈ F, ∀ y ∈ F, B (J₁ x) y = -B x (J₁ y))
hypotheses.justification: It follows from the other hypotheses. From `hlin` one gets subtraction-additivity in the first argument on F (exactly the file's `hBsub`: take z = -1 in `hlin` and use `neg_add_eq_sub`), and then, together with `hsymm` and `map_sub`, `hBsub'` in the second argument (the file itself proves `hBsub'` at line 386-387 using only `hlin`, `hsymm`). With those, for x ∈ F, y ∈ F: `h23` gives `J₁ x = J₂ (J₃ x) - J₃ (J₂ x)`; hence B (J₁ x) y = B (J₂ (J₃ x)) y - B (J₃ (J₂ x)) y (uses hBsub, hF₃ x hx, hF₂ x hx) = -B (J₃ x) (J₂ y) + B (J₂ x) (J₃ y) (hskew₂ at J₃ x, hskew₃ at J₂ x) = B x (J₃ (J₂ y)) - B x (J₂ (J₃ y)) (hskew₃ at x, J₂ y; hskew₂ at x, J₃ y) = -B x (J₂ (J₃ y) - J₃ (J₂ y)) (hBsub', hF₂ y hy, hF₃ y hy) = -B x (J₁ y) (by `h23 y hy`). So after deleting `hskew₁` one re-derives it from `h23`, `hskew₂`, `hskew₃`, `hlin`, `hsymm` and applies the same proof. In the proof `hskew₁` is used only in `hadjp`/`hadjm` (lines 450, 455), so nothing else changes. This argument needs `hskew₂` and `hskew₃`, so at most one of the three skewness hypotheses can be dropped at a time (this one can be dropped only if the other two stay).

hypotheses.binder: (hskew₂ : ∀ x ∈ F, ∀ y ∈ F, B (J₂ x) y = -B x (J₂ y))
hypotheses.justification: It follows from the other hypotheses. Using the first- and second-argument subtraction additivity on F obtained from `hlin` and `hsymm` (the file's `hBsub`, `hBsub'`), and `h31` (`J₂ x = J₃ (J₁ x) - J₁ (J₃ x)`): B (J₂ x) y = B (J₃ (J₁ x)) y - B (J₁ (J₃ x)) y (hBsub, hF₁, hF₃) = -B (J₁ x) (J₃ y) + B (J₃ x) (J₁ y) (hskew₃ at J₁ x; hskew₁ at J₃ x) = B x (J₁ (J₃ y)) - B x (J₃ (J₁ y)) (hskew₁ at x, J₃ y; hskew₃ at x, J₁ y) = -B x (J₃ (J₁ y) - J₁ (J₃ y)) (hBsub') = -B x (J₂ y) (by `h31 y hy`). Then the unchanged proof (where `hskew₂` is used only in `hadjp`/`hadjm`, lines 450 and 455) applies to the re-derived `hskew₂`. This uses `hskew₁` and `hskew₃`, so it cannot be combined with deleting either of those.

hypotheses.binder: (hskew₃ : ∀ x ∈ F, ∀ y ∈ F, B (J₃ x) y = -B x (J₃ y))
hypotheses.justification: It follows from the other hypotheses: `h12` expresses J₃ as the commutator `J₁ J₂ - J₂ J₁` on F, and the skewness of J₁ and J₂ then transfers to J₃. Concretely, with the first/second-argument subtraction additivity on F derived from `hlin` and `hsymm` (the file's `hBsub`, `hBsub'`): B (J₃ x) y = B (J₁ (J₂ x) - J₂ (J₁ x)) y (by `h12 x hx`, hF₁, hF₂ for membership) = B (J₁ (J₂ x)) y - B (J₂ (J₁ x)) y = -B (J₂ x) (J₁ y) + B (J₁ x) (J₂ y) (hskew₁ at J₂ x, hskew₂ at J₁ x) = B x (J₂ (J₁ y)) - B x (J₁ (J₂ y)) (hskew₂ at x, J₁ y; hskew₁ at x, J₂ y) = -B x (J₁ (J₂ y) - J₂ (J₁ y)) (hBsub') = -B x (J₃ y) (by `h12 y hy`). In the proof `hskew₃` is used only to prove `hLsymm` (line 407), so after re-deriving it the rest of the argument (`hbound`, `hspec`, `exists_eigen_decomposition`, final computation) is unchanged. This derivation needs `hskew₁` and `hskew₂`, so it cannot be combined with deleting either of them. (No claim is made about `[FiniteDimensional ℂ F]`: the current proof genuinely needs it through `exists_eigen_decomposition` with `Module.finrank ℂ F`.)
